title: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics (Final P3)
description: CA Final Paper 3 under the ICAI new scheme: quality control, Standards on Auditing, audit reports and CARO 2020, specialised assurance, bank and PSU audits, internal audit and forensic work, and professional ethics. Built for attempts from May 2027 with case-based MCQs and 'comment with reasons' theory practice.

chapters.title: Quality Control, Quality Management and SA 220
chapters.summary: How a CA firm builds a system of quality control under SQC 1, where SQM 1 and SQM 2 stand, and what SA 220 asks of the engagement partner on each audit.
chapters.applicableFor: May 2027 onward (ICAI new scheme, CA Final Paper 3)
chapters.lawAsOf: SQC 1 and SA 220 as issued by ICAI; SQM 1 and SQM 2 issued 14 October 2024, mandatory date deferred by ICAI announcement of 31 March 2026

lesson.heading: Two levels of quality: the firm and the engagement
lesson.body:
Audit quality is managed at two levels.

- **Firm level**: SQC 1, 'Quality Control for Firms that Perform Audits and Reviews of Historical Financial Information, and Other Assurance and Related Services Engagements'. It requires every firm to design a system of quality control and document its policies and procedures.
- **Engagement level**: SA 220, 'Quality Control for an Audit of Financial Statements'. It places responsibility for the quality of each audit on the **engagement partner**.

SQC 1 lists six elements of the system of quality control:

| Element | What the firm must have |
| --- | --- |
| Leadership responsibilities for quality | A culture where quality comes first; ultimate responsibility with the managing partner or board |
| Relevant ethical requirements | Policies on independence, with written confirmation of independence from all personnel at least annually |
| Acceptance and continuance | Accept only clients where the firm is competent, can comply with ethics and has considered the integrity of the client |
| Human resources | Recruitment, training, assignment of engagement teams, performance evaluation |
| Engagement performance | Direction, supervision, review, consultation, engagement quality control review (EQCR), resolving differences of opinion |
| Monitoring | Ongoing evaluation and periodic inspection of completed engagements |

lesson.heading: Key SQC 1 requirements examiners test
lesson.body:
- **EQCR**: mandatory for all audits of financial statements of **listed entities**. For other engagements the firm sets criteria (public interest, unusual risk, law). The reviewer must be objective and must not be a member of the engagement team.
- **Long association**: for listed-entity audits the firm must have policies requiring rotation of the engagement partner after a specified period, not exceeding seven years under SQC 1. Section 139(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 separately limits auditor tenure for listed and prescribed companies (one term of 5 years for an individual, two terms of 5 years for a firm, followed by a 5-year cooling-off).
- **Engagement documentation**: the firm sets a retention period of **not less than seven years** from the date of the auditor's report (or, if later, the group auditor's report). SA 230 requires final assembly of the audit file within **60 days** after the date of the auditor's report.
- **Monitoring**: inspection of at least one completed engagement for each engagement partner on a cyclical basis. People who performed the engagement or its EQCR must not inspect it.
- **Complaints and allegations**: the firm needs a channel for complaints about non-compliance, including from its own staff, without fear of reprisal.

Working papers are the property of the auditor. The auditor may, at discretion, make portions available to the client, but is not obliged to.

lesson.heading: SQM 1 and SQM 2: status for your attempt
lesson.body:
ICAI issued **SQM 1** ('Quality Management for Firms that Perform Audits or Reviews of Financial Statements, or Other Assurance or Related Services Engagements') and **SQM 2** ('Engagement Quality Reviews') on 14 October 2024. They were to become mandatory from 1 April 2026, replacing SQC 1.

By an announcement dated 31 March 2026 (451st Council meeting), ICAI **deferred the mandatory date until further announcement**. Until then **SQC 1 continues to apply**. Firms may still adopt SQM voluntarily. Check the ICAI website before your exam for any new date.

What changes under SQM 1:

| SQC 1 | SQM 1 |
| --- | --- |
| Six elements, largely policy-driven | Eight components, risk-based |
| Firm writes policies and procedures | Firm sets quality objectives, identifies quality risks and designs responses |
| Monitoring by periodic inspection | Monitoring and remediation process with root cause analysis |
| EQCR inside SQC 1 | Engagement quality review moved to a separate standard, SQM 2 |

The eight SQM 1 components: governance and leadership; the firm's risk assessment process; relevant ethical requirements; acceptance and continuance; engagement performance; resources (human, technological, intellectual); information and communication; and the monitoring and remediation process. SQM 2 covers appointment and eligibility of the engagement quality reviewer, including a cooling-off period before a former engagement partner can act as reviewer.

lesson.heading: SA 220: the engagement partner's job
lesson.body:
SA 220 requires the engagement partner to:

- Take responsibility for the overall quality of each audit assigned.
- Remain alert for non-compliance with ethical requirements and form a conclusion on **independence**, taking action to remove threats or withdraw.
- Be satisfied that acceptance and continuance procedures were followed and conclusions are appropriate.
- Be satisfied that the team collectively has the competence and time needed.
- Take responsibility for direction, supervision and review, and for consultation on difficult or contentious matters.
- For audits needing an EQCR, discuss significant matters with the reviewer and **not date the auditor's report until the EQCR is complete**.
- Not date the report until any **difference of opinion** within the team, with consultees or with the EQC reviewer is resolved under firm policy.

The EQC reviewer evaluates significant judgements: discussion with the partner, review of the financial statements and proposed report, review of selected working papers, and evaluation of the conclusions reached.

lesson.heading: Answering 'comment with reasons' questions in this area
lesson.body:
A four-step format scores well:

- State the correct position in one line (correct / not correct).
- Quote the provision: SQC 1, SA 220, SA 230 or section of the Companies Act, 2013.
- Apply it to the facts in the question.
- Conclude, and say what the auditor should do.

Common mistakes:

- Saying EQCR is mandatory for every company audit. It is mandatory for listed entities; for others the firm sets criteria.
- Confusing the 60-day assembly period (SA 230) with the 7-year retention period (SQC 1).
- Writing that SQM 1 is already mandatory. For May 2027 attempts, state that SQC 1 continues until ICAI announces a new date.
- Treating the EQC reviewer as a second engagement partner. The reviewer does not reduce the engagement partner's responsibility.

keyPoints: SQC 1 = firm-level quality control (6 elements); SA 220 = engagement-level quality control by the engagement partner.
EQCR is mandatory for audits of listed entities; report cannot be dated before EQCR is complete.
Documentation retention: not less than 7 years (SQC 1); file assembly within 60 days of report date (SA 230).
Independence confirmations in writing from all personnel at least annually.
SQM 1 (8 components, risk-based) and SQM 2 (engagement quality reviews) issued October 2024; mandatory date deferred on 31 March 2026, so SQC 1 continues.
Partner rotation for listed audits under SQC 1: specified period not exceeding 7 years; tenure limits under section 139(2) apply separately.

cases.title: Case: Mehta Rao and Associates
cases.body:
Mehta Rao and Associates (MRA) is a 6-partner firm in Pune. For FY 2025-26 it audits Deccan Polymers Ltd, a company listed on NSE. CA Kiran Mehta has been the engagement partner for Deccan Polymers for eight consecutive years.

Facts gathered during an internal review:

| Item | Fact |
| --- | --- |
| EQCR | Not performed because the reviewing partner was on leave; report signed and dated on 20 May 2026 |
| Article assistant Neha | Holds 400 shares of Deccan Polymers; did not disclose them in the annual independence declaration |
| File assembly | Audit file of Deccan Polymers assembled on 5 August 2026 |
| Retention policy | Firm manual says audit files are destroyed after 5 years |
| Monitoring | No completed engagement of Kiran Mehta has been inspected in the last 5 years |

questions.prompt: Which standard places responsibility for the quality of an individual audit on the engagement partner?
questions.explanation: SA 220 deals with quality control at the engagement level and makes the engagement partner responsible for the overall quality of each audit. SQC 1 operates at firm level, SA 230 covers documentation and SQM 2 covers engagement quality reviews.

questions.prompt: Under SQC 1, an engagement quality control review is mandatory for:
options: Audits of financial statements of listed entities
questions.explanation: SQC 1 makes EQCR mandatory for all audits of financial statements of listed entities. For other engagements, the firm sets its own criteria based on public interest, risk or legal requirements.

questions.prompt: As per the ICAI announcement of 31 March 2026, what is the status of SQM 1 and SQM 2?
options: Mandatory date deferred until further announcement; SQC 1 continues to apply
Mandatory only for listed-entity audits from 1 April 2026
questions.explanation: ICAI deferred the compulsory implementation date of SQM 1 and SQM 2 until further announcement, and stated that SQC 1 continues to remain applicable in the meantime.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a component of SQM 1 but not a separate element of SQC 1?
questions.explanation: SQM 1 adds a risk assessment process (setting quality objectives, identifying quality risks and designing responses) and an information and communication component. The other three appear in both standards.

questions.prompt: What is the correct view on the Deccan Polymers auditor's report dated 20 May 2026?
options: Valid, because EQCR is optional when the reviewer is unavailable
Not in line with SA 220, because for a listed entity the report should not be dated until the EQCR is complete
Valid, because the engagement partner alone is responsible for the opinion
Not in line with SA 230, because the file was assembled late
questions.explanation: Deccan Polymers is listed, so EQCR is mandatory. SA 220 says the engagement partner shall not date the report until the EQCR is completed. The firm should have assigned another eligible reviewer.

questions.prompt: Neha's shareholding in Deccan Polymers primarily indicates a weakness in which SQC 1 element?
questions.explanation: SQC 1 requires the firm to obtain written confirmation of independence from all personnel at least annually. An undisclosed financial interest in an audit client is an independence failure under relevant ethical requirements.

questions.prompt: Which two facts breach SA 230 and SQC 1 respectively?
options: Assembly on 5 August 2026 (beyond 60 days) and 5-year retention policy (below 7 years)
Assembly on 5 August 2026 and Neha's shareholding
5-year retention policy and absence of EQCR
Eight-year tenure and the monitoring gap
questions.explanation: The report is dated 20 May 2026; 60 days later is 19 July 2026, so assembly on 5 August is late under SA 230. SQC 1 requires retention of at least 7 years from the report date, so a 5-year policy is non-compliant.

questions.prompt: The engagement quality control reviewer shares responsibility for the audit opinion with the engagement partner.
questions.explanation: The EQC reviewer gives an objective evaluation of significant judgements. Responsibility for the engagement and the opinion stays with the engagement partner.

questions.prompt: Kiran Mehta continuing as engagement partner for an eighth year on a listed-entity audit is consistent with SQC 1's rotation policy requirement.
questions.explanation: SQC 1 requires rotation of the engagement partner on listed-entity audits after a specified period not exceeding seven years. An eighth consecutive year breaches it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are procedures an EQC reviewer performs? Select all that apply.
options: Discussing significant matters with the engagement partner
Reviewing the financial statements and the proposed auditor's report
Reviewing selected working papers on significant judgements
Signing the auditor's report jointly with the partner
questions.explanation: EQCR is an objective evaluation of significant judgements through discussion, review of the financial statements and report, and review of selected documentation. The reviewer does not re-perform the audit or sign the report.

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: under SA 230, the auditor completes the assembly of the final audit file within ___ days after the date of the auditor's report.
questions.explanation: SA 230 sets an appropriate time limit for final file assembly as not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor's report.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'Since SQM 1 was issued in October 2024, SQC 1 no longer applies to audit firms for FY 2026-27.'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- ICAI issued SQM 1 and SQM 2 on 14 October 2024 with a planned mandatory date of 1 April 2026.
- By its announcement dated 31 March 2026, ICAI deferred the mandatory effective date until further announcement.
- The announcement states that SQC 1 continues to remain applicable until then.
- A firm may adopt SQM 1 voluntarily, but it must still meet SQC 1.

Conclusion: SQC 1 applies for FY 2026-27 unless ICAI notifies a new date.

questions.prompt: Explain the elements of a system of quality control under SQC 1.
questions.answer:
SQC 1 requires a firm to establish policies and procedures on six elements:

- **Leadership responsibilities**: a culture that puts quality first, led by the managing partner.
- **Relevant ethical requirements**: independence policies and annual written confirmations.
- **Acceptance and continuance**: integrity of the client, competence and capability of the firm, ability to comply with ethics.
- **Human resources**: recruitment, training, assignment of teams, evaluation.
- **Engagement performance**: supervision, review, consultation, EQCR, resolving differences of opinion, documentation.
- **Monitoring**: ongoing evaluation and cyclical inspection of completed engagements of each partner.

The firm documents these policies and communicates them to personnel.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'During the audit of an unlisted company, the audit manager and the engagement partner disagree on the valuation of inventory. The partner signs the report anyway because the final decision is his.'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- SA 220 requires that where differences of opinion arise within the engagement team, with consultees or with the EQC reviewer, the team follows the firm's policies for dealing with and resolving them.
- The engagement partner shall not date the auditor's report until the matter is resolved.
- SQC 1 requires the firm to have such policies, with the conclusions documented and implemented.

Conclusion: the partner should consult as per firm policy, document the resolution, and only then date and sign the report.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'The client asked CA Suresh to hand over his complete audit working papers since the client paid the audit fee. Suresh must comply.'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- Under SQC 1 (and SA 230), audit documentation is the property of the auditor.
- The auditor may, at his discretion, make portions or extracts available to the client, provided this does not undermine the validity of the work or the independence of the firm.
- Payment of fees does not transfer ownership of working papers.
- The firm must also maintain confidentiality, safe custody and retention for at least 7 years.

Conclusion: Suresh is not bound to hand over the papers; he may share extracts at his discretion.

chapters.title: Auditor's Responsibilities: Fraud, Laws, Communication and Joint Audit
chapters.summary: The auditor's duties on fraud (SA 240 and section 143(12)), laws and regulations (SA 250), communication with those charged with governance (SA 260, SA 265) and joint audits (SA 299).
chapters.applicableFor: May 2027 onward (ICAI new scheme, CA Final Paper 3)
chapters.lawAsOf: SA 240, 250, 260, 265 and SA 299 (Revised) as issued by ICAI; Companies Act, 2013 section 143(12) read with Rule 13 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014

lesson.heading: SA 240: fraud in an audit of financial statements
lesson.body:
Primary responsibility for preventing and detecting fraud rests with **management and those charged with governance (TCWG)**. The auditor obtains reasonable assurance that the financial statements are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.

Two types of fraud matter to the auditor:

- **Fraudulent financial reporting**: intentional misstatement or omission, for example fictitious revenue, improper cut-off, hiding liabilities.
- **Misappropriation of assets**: theft of cash, inventory or other assets, often hidden by false records.

Key requirements:

- Maintain **professional skepticism** throughout, even if past experience suggests management is honest.
- **Engagement team discussion** on where the financial statements are susceptible to fraud.
- **Presumed risk in revenue recognition**: the auditor presumes a fraud risk in revenue. This presumption is rebuttable, but the reasons must be documented.
- **Management override of controls** is a risk in every entity and cannot be rebutted. Mandatory responses: test journal entries and other adjustments, review accounting estimates for bias, and evaluate the business rationale of significant unusual transactions.
- If fraud makes it doubtful whether the audit can continue, consider withdrawal where permitted by law.

lesson.heading: Section 143(12): reporting fraud to the Central Government
lesson.body:
If the auditor, in the course of performing duties, has reason to believe that an offence of fraud involving the company is being or has been committed **against the company by its officers or employees**, Rule 13 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 sets the route:

| Amount of fraud | Auditor's action |
| --- | --- |
| ₹1 crore or above | Report to the Board or Audit Committee immediately, not later than 2 days of knowledge, seeking their reply within 45 days. Forward the report, with the reply or his comments, to the Central Government within 15 days of receiving the reply (or of expiry of 45 days). Form ADT-4. |
| Below ₹1 crore | Report to the Audit Committee or Board within 2 days of knowledge. The company discloses details in the Board's report. |

Notes:

- Fraud **by the company** against outsiders (for example tax evasion by the company) is not covered by section 143(12).
- The duty applies equally to cost auditors and secretarial auditors.
- Reporting in good faith is not a breach of the duty of confidentiality.

lesson.heading: SA 250: laws and regulations
lesson.body:
SA 250 divides laws into two categories:

| Category | Auditor's responsibility | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Laws with a **direct effect** on material amounts and disclosures | Obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence of compliance | Companies Act provisions on financial statements, income-tax, GST, PF and ESI dues |
| **Other laws** that are fundamental to operations | Limited procedures: inquiry of management and TCWG, inspection of correspondence with regulators | Pollution control laws, licensing laws, labour laws |

The auditor is not responsible for preventing non-compliance and cannot be expected to detect all of it. If non-compliance is identified or suspected, the auditor understands the nature and circumstances, evaluates the effect on the financial statements, discusses with management and TCWG, considers legal advice, and evaluates the effect on the opinion. Where law or regulation requires, the auditor reports to an outside authority.

lesson.heading: SA 260, SA 265 and SA 299
lesson.body:
**SA 260 (Communication with TCWG)**: the auditor communicates his responsibilities, the planned scope and timing, significant findings (difficulties, significant qualitative aspects of accounting practices, written representations requested, significant matters discussed with management) and, for listed entities, a statement on independence. Form can be oral or written; significant findings go in writing when oral communication would not be adequate.

**SA 265 (Communicating deficiencies in internal control)**: significant deficiencies are communicated **in writing** to TCWG on a timely basis. Other deficiencies of sufficient importance go to management. A **significant deficiency** is a deficiency or combination of deficiencies that, in the auditor's judgement, merits TCWG's attention.

**SA 299 (Revised), Joint Audit of Financial Statements**:

- Joint auditors agree the overall audit strategy and plan, and document the allocation of work in writing.
- Each joint auditor is responsible for the work allocated to him. All joint auditors are **jointly and severally responsible** for work not allocated and carried out jointly, for decisions taken jointly on the nature, timing and extent of procedures, and for the audit report.
- Joint auditors issue a common audit report. If they disagree on any matter, the auditor in disagreement expresses his opinion in a separate report.

lesson.heading: Exam technique and common mistakes
lesson.body:
- Do not say the auditor must detect all frauds. Inherent limitations (collusion, forgery, override) mean even a properly planned audit may not detect a material fraud.
- Do not apply section 143(12) to fraud by the company on third parties.
- Under section 143(12), the ₹1 crore threshold decides the route, not whether reporting is needed.
- In SA 299 answers, separate 'allocated work' (individual responsibility) from 'joint decisions and unallocated work' (joint and several responsibility).
- SA 265 communication of significant deficiencies is always in writing; SA 260 communication may be oral for routine matters.

keyPoints: Primary responsibility for fraud prevention and detection: management and TCWG (SA 240).
Revenue recognition fraud risk is a rebuttable presumption; management override risk is not rebuttable.
Section 143(12): fraud ≥ ₹1 crore by officers or employees goes to the Central Government in ADT-4 (2 days, 45 days, 15 days); below ₹1 crore goes to Audit Committee or Board within 2 days.
SA 250: direct-effect laws need sufficient appropriate evidence; other laws need limited procedures.
SA 265: significant deficiencies in internal control communicated in writing to TCWG.
SA 299: allocated work = individual responsibility; joint decisions, unallocated work and the report = joint and several.

cases.title: Case: Kaveri Textiles Ltd
cases.body:
Kaveri Textiles Ltd, an unlisted public company in Coimbatore, is audited jointly by Iyer and Co. and Bose Mitra LLP for FY 2025-26. The written allocation gives receivables and revenue to Iyer and Co. and inventory and fixed assets to Bose Mitra LLP. Taxation was not allocated and was audited jointly.

During fieldwork on 12 June 2026, Iyer and Co. finds:

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Fictitious sales | Sales head booked sales of ₹1,80,00,000 to non-existent parties to earn incentives; the amount is reversed in the next month |
| Cash shortage | A cashier misappropriated ₹6,50,000 over the year |
| Pollution notice | State Pollution Control Board notice proposing closure of one dyeing unit |
| GST dues | GST of ₹22,00,000 unpaid for 7 months |

Bose Mitra LLP did not look at revenue at all.

questions.prompt: Under SA 240, which fraud risk can never be rebutted by the auditor?
options: Risk of fraud in revenue recognition
Risk of management override of controls
Risk of fraud in inventory valuation
questions.explanation: Management override of controls is present in all entities, so SA 240 treats it as a significant risk that cannot be rebutted. The revenue presumption can be rebutted with documented reasons.

questions.prompt: Under SA 250, for 'other laws' that do not have a direct effect on the financial statements, the auditor's procedures are limited to:
options: Obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence of full compliance
Inquiring of management and TCWG and inspecting correspondence with regulatory authorities
Obtaining a legal opinion in every case
questions.explanation: For other laws, SA 250 requires specified procedures to help identify non-compliance: inquiry of management and TCWG and inspection of correspondence with licensing or regulatory authorities.

questions.prompt: A significant deficiency in internal control must be communicated by the auditor:
options: In writing to TCWG on a timely basis
questions.explanation: SA 265 requires written communication of significant deficiencies to those charged with governance on a timely basis.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT covered by the reporting duty under section 143(12)?
options: Inflated expense claims by a director
Evasion of customs duty by the company
Theft of inventory by warehouse staff
questions.explanation: Section 143(12) covers fraud committed against the company by its officers or employees. Duty evasion by the company itself is fraud by the company, which is outside section 143(12).

questions.prompt: For the fictitious sales of ₹1,80,00,000, what should Iyer and Co. do under section 143(12)?
options: Report to the Central Government directly within 2 days
Report to the Board or Audit Committee within 2 days, seek a reply within 45 days, then forward to the Central Government within 15 days in ADT-4
Only mention it in the CARO report
Nothing, since the sales are reversed next month
questions.explanation: The fraud is by an officer against the company and is ₹1 crore or more, so the Rule 13 route applies: Board or Audit Committee within 2 days, reply within 45 days, then the Central Government within 15 days in Form ADT-4. Reversal does not remove the fraud.

questions.prompt: How should the cashier's misappropriation of ₹6,50,000 be handled under section 143(12)?
options: Report to the Central Government in ADT-4
Report to the Audit Committee or Board within 2 days; the company discloses it in the Board's report
questions.explanation: Frauds below ₹1 crore are reported by the auditor to the Audit Committee or Board within 2 days of knowledge, and the company discloses them in the Board's report.

questions.prompt: Bose Mitra LLP did not examine revenue. Under SA 299 (Revised), for which area is it jointly and severally responsible?
options: Revenue, since all joint auditors are responsible for everything
Taxation, which was not allocated and was audited jointly
Only inventory and fixed assets, nothing else
None, since responsibility is always divided
questions.explanation: Each joint auditor is responsible for the work allocated to it. Work not allocated and done jointly, joint decisions and the audit report carry joint and several responsibility. Revenue was allocated to Iyer and Co.

questions.prompt: Under SA 240, if the auditor has found management honest in earlier audits, he may reduce professional skepticism in the current audit.
questions.explanation: SA 240 requires professional skepticism throughout the audit, recognising that fraud could exist despite past experience of management's honesty and integrity.

questions.prompt: Unpaid GST of ₹22,00,000 relates to a law with a direct effect on the financial statements, so the auditor must obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about it.
questions.explanation: Tax laws determine amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, so they fall in the first category under SA 250. The default is also reportable under CARO 2020 clause (vii).

questions.prompt: Which procedures does SA 240 require in response to the risk of management override of controls? Select all that apply.
options: Testing the appropriateness of journal entries and other adjustments
Evaluating the business rationale of significant unusual transactions
questions.explanation: These three procedures are required in every audit regardless of the assessed risk of override. A forensic audit and blanket bank confirmations are not required responses under SA 240.

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: the form in which an auditor reports a fraud of ₹1 crore or more to the Central Government is Form ___.
questions.explanation: Rule 13(2) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 prescribes Form ADT-4.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'An auditor who did not detect a material fraud has necessarily failed to comply with the Standards on Auditing.'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- SA 200 and SA 240 recognise inherent limitations: an audit gives reasonable, not absolute, assurance.
- Fraud may involve sophisticated schemes, forgery, collusion or management override designed to conceal it.
- The risk of not detecting fraud is higher than for error, and higher for management fraud than employee fraud.
- Whether the auditor complied with SAs depends on the procedures performed, the sufficiency and appropriateness of evidence and the skepticism shown, not on the outcome.

Conclusion: non-detection alone does not prove non-compliance, though it may lead to an inquiry into whether the audit was properly conducted.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'The statutory auditor of Rajat Ltd found that the company had evaded GST of ₹3 crore by suppressing sales. He must report it to the Central Government under section 143(12).'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- Section 143(12) applies to fraud against the company by its officers or employees.
- Here the fraud is committed by the company itself (against the government revenue), so section 143(12) does not apply.
- The auditor deals with it under SA 250 (non-compliance with a direct-effect law): evaluate the effect on the financial statements (tax, interest, penalty provisions and contingent liabilities), communicate with TCWG, and consider the effect on the opinion.
- The matter may also be reportable under CARO 2020 (statutory dues and unrecorded income clauses), if applicable.

Conclusion: no ADT-4 reporting, but audit consequences follow.

questions.prompt: Explain the responsibilities of joint auditors under SA 299 (Revised).
questions.answer:
- Joint auditors jointly plan the audit, agree the overall strategy and allocate work, documenting the division in writing and communicating it to TCWG.
- Each joint auditor is responsible only for the work allocated to him, including proper execution and reporting.
- All joint auditors are jointly and severally responsible for: work not divided and carried out jointly; decisions on nature, timing and extent of procedures taken jointly; matters brought to their notice by another joint auditor and discussed; and the auditor's report and its compliance with law.
- Each joint auditor may rely on the others' work, but must discuss significant observations.
- A common report is issued; a joint auditor who disagrees issues a separate report.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'The auditor told the managing director orally about a significant deficiency in the approval of credit notes. This meets the requirement of SA 265.'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- SA 265 requires significant deficiencies in internal control to be communicated in writing to those charged with governance, on a timely basis.
- Communication to management (the managing director) alone, orally, does not meet the requirement, unless the MD is also the only person charged with governance and even then it must be in writing.
- The written communication includes a description of the deficiency, its potential effects and enough information for TCWG to understand that the audit was not designed to express an opinion on internal control.

Conclusion: the auditor should send a written communication to TCWG.

chapters.title: Audit Planning, Strategy and Execution
chapters.summary: Planning under SA 300, risk assessment under SA 315, materiality under SA 320, responses under SA 330 and evaluation of misstatements under SA 450.
chapters.applicableFor: May 2027 onward (ICAI new scheme, CA Final Paper 3)
chapters.lawAsOf: SA 300, SA 315, SA 320, SA 330 and SA 450 as issued by ICAI

lesson.heading: SA 300: overall audit strategy and audit plan
lesson.body:
Planning is a continual process, not a one-time phase. It starts after the previous audit ends and continues until the current audit is complete.

| Overall audit strategy | Audit plan |
| --- | --- |
| Sets the scope, timing and direction of the audit | Detailed: nature, timing and extent of risk assessment procedures, further procedures and other procedures |
| Considers reporting objectives, significant factors, preliminary engagement activities, nature and extent of resources | Prepared by applying the strategy |
| Prepared first | Updated as the audit progresses |

Preliminary engagement activities: SA 220 procedures on continuance, evaluation of ethical requirements including independence, and agreeing terms under SA 210.

For an **initial audit engagement**, additional activities include communicating with the predecessor auditor (subject to ethical requirements), and procedures on opening balances under SA 510.

lesson.heading: SA 315 and SA 330: assess risks, then respond
lesson.body:
**Risk assessment procedures** (SA 315): inquiries of management and others, analytical procedures, and observation and inspection. They give the auditor an understanding of the entity, its environment, the applicable financial reporting framework and its system of internal control.

Risks of material misstatement (RoMM) are assessed at two levels:

- **Financial statement level**: pervasive risks, for example weak control environment or going-concern pressure.
- **Assertion level**: for classes of transactions, account balances and disclosures. RoMM = inherent risk x control risk.

A **significant risk** needs special audit consideration. For significant risks, the auditor must understand related controls and must perform substantive procedures specifically responsive to the risk; if only substantive procedures are used, they must include tests of details.

**SA 330 responses**:

- Overall responses to financial-statement-level risks: more experienced staff, more supervision, more unpredictability, changes to timing.
- Further audit procedures at assertion level: **tests of controls** (when relying on controls or when substantive procedures alone are insufficient) and **substantive procedures** (tests of details and substantive analytical procedures).
- Irrespective of assessed risk, substantive procedures are required for each **material** class of transactions, account balance and disclosure.
- If relying on controls tested in a prior audit (and unchanged), test them at least **once in every third audit**. Controls over significant risks must be tested in the current period.

lesson.heading: SA 320 and SA 450: materiality and misstatements
lesson.body:
**Materiality for the financial statements as a whole** is set using a benchmark and a percentage based on professional judgement, for example a percentage of profit before tax from continuing operations, revenue, total assets or equity.

**Performance materiality** is set lower than overall materiality, to reduce to an appropriately low level the probability that aggregate uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceed materiality. Materiality is revised if information comes to light during the audit that would have caused a different amount.

Worked example:

| Particulars | Amount (₹) |
| --- | --- |
| Profit before tax | 8,40,00,000 |
| Overall materiality at 5% | 42,00,000 |
| Performance materiality at 75% of overall | 31,50,000 |
| Clearly trivial threshold at 5% of overall | 2,10,000 |

**SA 450** requires the auditor to accumulate all misstatements other than those that are clearly trivial. Misstatements are:

- **Factual**: no doubt about them.
- **Judgemental**: differences in judgements on estimates or policies.
- **Projected**: the auditor's best estimate in a population from a sample.

The auditor communicates misstatements to management on a timely basis and requests correction. Uncorrected misstatements are communicated to TCWG and a **written representation** is obtained that management believes their effect is immaterial, with a summary attached.

lesson.heading: Common mistakes
lesson.body:
- Treating materiality as a fixed percentage required by the SA. SA 320 gives examples; the choice is judgement.
- Concluding 'no substantive procedures needed' because controls are strong. Substantive procedures are always required for material items.
- Ignoring qualitative factors. A small misstatement can be material if it turns a profit into a loss, affects a covenant, or involves fraud or related parties.
- Ignoring projected misstatements when evaluating whether aggregate uncorrected misstatements are material.
- Assuming strategy and plan are prepared once. SA 300 requires updating both as the audit progresses.

keyPoints: SA 300: overall audit strategy (scope, timing, direction) comes first; the audit plan details procedures. Both are updated during the audit.
SA 315 risk assessment procedures: inquiry, analytical procedures, observation and inspection.
Significant risk: understand related controls; substantive procedures specific to the risk (tests of details if purely substantive).
SA 330: substantive procedures for every material class, balance and disclosure; controls relied on from prior audits tested at least once in every third audit.
Performance materiality is lower than overall materiality; materiality is revised when new information arises.
SA 450: misstatements are factual, judgemental or projected; obtain written representation on uncorrected misstatements.

cases.title: Case: Sunrise Pharma Ltd
cases.body:
CA Anjali Desai audits Sunrise Pharma Ltd for FY 2025-26. Overall materiality is ₹50,00,000 and the clearly trivial threshold is ₹2,50,000. At the completion stage the summary of misstatements is:

| Ref | Nature | Amount (₹) | Management's response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Inventory overstated: goods received after year end included in closing stock | 18,00,000 | Corrected |
| B | Warranty provision lower than the auditor's estimate | 12,00,000 | Not corrected |
| C | Purchases: sample error extrapolated to the population | 9,00,000 | Not corrected |
| D | Telephone expense wrongly classified | 1,50,000 | Not corrected |

The company has a loan covenant that requires profit before tax of at least ₹6,00,00,000. Draft profit before tax after correcting A is ₹6,15,00,000.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is part of the overall audit strategy rather than the audit plan?
options: Sample sizes for testing trade receivables
Determining the reporting deadlines and nature of resources to be deployed
Selection of specific items for bank reconciliation testing
questions.explanation: The strategy sets scope, timing and direction, including reporting objectives and resources. Sample sizes and detailed steps belong to the audit plan.

questions.prompt: Under SA 330, if the auditor plans to rely on controls tested in a prior audit and those controls have not changed, they must be tested:
options: At least once in every third audit
questions.explanation: SA 330 allows reliance on audit evidence from prior audits for unchanged controls, but requires testing at least once in every third audit, and some controls each audit. Controls over significant risks are tested every period.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a risk assessment procedure under SA 315?
questions.explanation: SA 315 lists inquiries, analytical procedures and observation and inspection as risk assessment procedures. External confirmation is a further (substantive) procedure under SA 505.

questions.prompt: Profit before tax of Vega Ltd is ₹8,40,00,000. The auditor sets overall materiality at 5% of profit before tax and performance materiality at 75% of overall materiality. Performance materiality is:
questions.explanation:
| Step | Amount (₹) |
| --- | --- |
| Overall materiality = 5% x 8,40,00,000 | 42,00,000 |
| Performance materiality = 75% x 42,00,000 | 31,50,000 |

questions.prompt: Compute the aggregate of uncorrected misstatements that the auditor must accumulate and evaluate, in ₹ (round to the nearest rupee).
questions.explanation:
A is corrected. D (₹1,50,000) is below the clearly trivial threshold of ₹2,50,000, so it is not accumulated.

| Item | Amount (₹) |
| --- | --- |
| B Judgemental | 12,00,000 |
| C Projected | 9,00,000 |
| **Aggregate uncorrected** | **21,00,000** |

questions.prompt: How are misstatements B and C classified under SA 450?
questions.explanation: B arises from a difference in judgement on an estimate (warranty provision). C is the auditor's best estimate of misstatement in a population based on a sample, which is a projected misstatement.

questions.prompt: Aggregate uncorrected misstatements are below overall materiality. What should Anjali consider before concluding?
options: Qualitative factors: if B and C (both reduce profit) are corrected, profit before tax falls below the ₹6,00,00,000 covenant
She must issue a qualified opinion
She must revise materiality upward to ₹1,00,00,000
questions.explanation: Profit of ₹6,15,00,000 less ₹21,00,000 is ₹5,94,00,000, which breaches the covenant. SA 450 and SA 320 require the auditor to consider qualitative factors such as covenant compliance, so these misstatements may be material by nature.

questions.prompt: If the auditor assesses control risk as low for all assertions, SA 330 permits him to skip substantive procedures for material account balances.
questions.explanation: Irrespective of the assessed risk, SA 330 requires substantive procedures for each material class of transactions, account balance and disclosure, because risk assessment is judgemental and controls have inherent limitations.

questions.prompt: Anjali should obtain a written representation that management believes the effect of uncorrected misstatements B and C is immaterial, with a summary of those items attached.
questions.explanation: SA 450 requires a written representation from management and, where appropriate, TCWG on whether they believe the effects of uncorrected misstatements are immaterial, with a summary included in or attached to the representation.

questions.prompt: Which are appropriate overall responses under SA 330 to a high risk of material misstatement at the financial statement level? Select all that apply.
options: Assigning more experienced staff or specialists
Adding unpredictability to the selection of procedures
Reducing sample sizes to finish quickly
Relying more on management's internal reports
questions.explanation: SA 330 lists emphasising skepticism, experienced staff, more supervision, unpredictability and changes in timing or extent. Smaller samples or more reliance on management reports would increase audit risk.

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: the amount set below overall materiality to reduce the probability that aggregate uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceed materiality is called ___ materiality.
questions.explanation: SA 320 defines performance materiality for this purpose.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'Audit planning is completed before fieldwork begins and is not revisited.'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- SA 300 states that planning is a continual and iterative process, beginning soon after the previous audit and continuing until completion of the current audit.
- The overall audit strategy and audit plan are updated and changed as necessary during the audit, for example when unexpected events occur, conditions change or evidence contradicts earlier assessments.
- SA 315 and SA 330 also require revision of risk assessments when new evidence arises, and SA 320 requires revision of materiality.
- Significant changes and reasons are documented.

Conclusion: planning is revisited throughout the audit.

questions.prompt: Explain what a significant risk is and how the auditor responds to it.
questions.answer:
- A significant risk is an identified risk of material misstatement that, in the auditor's judgement, requires special audit consideration (for example non-routine transactions, complex estimates, fraud risks including revenue and management override).
- The auditor obtains an understanding of the entity's controls relevant to that risk, including control activities.
- If relying on controls over a significant risk, they are tested in the current period (no reliance on prior-year evidence).
- Substantive procedures specifically responsive to the risk are performed; if the approach is only substantive, it includes tests of details.
- The risk and responses are documented and communicated to TCWG where relevant (SA 260).

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'Since the telephone expense misclassification of ₹40,000 is below materiality, the auditor need not record it.'
questions.answer:
Partly correct, depending on the clearly trivial threshold.

- SA 450 requires the auditor to accumulate all misstatements identified during the audit other than those that are clearly trivial.
- 'Clearly trivial' is a much smaller amount than materiality; it is matters clearly inconsequential individually and in aggregate.
- If ₹40,000 is above the clearly trivial threshold, it must be accumulated, communicated to management and evaluated with other misstatements, even though it is below materiality.
- If it is below the clearly trivial threshold, it need not be accumulated.

Conclusion: being below materiality is not the test; the test is whether it is clearly trivial.

questions.prompt: What additional planning activities does SA 300 require for an initial audit engagement?
questions.answer:
- Arrangements with the predecessor auditor, such as reviewing working papers, subject to ethical requirements and the predecessor's consent.
- Communication with the predecessor auditor before acceptance, as required by the Code of Ethics and Clause (8) of Part I of the First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949.
- Discussion with management of major issues (accounting policies, standards, reporting) that affected the decision to accept.
- Procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence on opening balances (SA 510).
- Other procedures under the firm's quality control system, such as involving another partner to review the strategy before starting significant procedures.

resources.title: ICAI: Auditing and Assurance Standards Board

chapters.title: Internal Control in an IT Environment and Data Analytics
chapters.summary: Components of internal control, IT general controls and application controls, the audit trail requirement under the Companies Act, internal financial controls reporting, and using data analytics in audits.
chapters.applicableFor: May 2027 onward (ICAI new scheme, CA Final Paper 3)
chapters.lawAsOf: SA 315 and SA 330 as issued by ICAI; Companies Act, 2013 section 143(3)(i); proviso to Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 and Rule 11(g) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014

lesson.heading: Internal control and the IT environment
lesson.body:
SA 315 describes five components of internal control:

| Component | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Control environment | Tone at the top, board oversight, HR policies |
| Entity's risk assessment process | How management identifies business risks relevant to reporting |
| Process to monitor the system of internal control | Internal audit, periodic reviews |
| Information system and communication | ERP, chart of accounts, period-end close process |
| Control activities | Authorisation, reconciliations, segregation of duties, IT controls |

In an IT environment, risks include unauthorised access to data, unauthorised changes to programs or master data, failure to make necessary changes, inappropriate manual intervention, and loss of data. IT also brings benefits: consistent processing, automated calculations and reports, and reduced risk of circumvention.

lesson.heading: IT general controls and application controls
lesson.body:
**IT general controls (ITGCs)** support the continued functioning of application controls across systems:

- **Access security**: user creation, password policies, privileged access, periodic access reviews.
- **Program change management**: request, test, approve, and move changes to production by someone other than the developer.
- **Program development and acquisition**: testing and approval of new systems and data migration.
- **IT operations**: job scheduling, backups, incident management.

**Application controls** operate within a specific application and work at the transaction level:

- Input: validation checks, limit checks, field checks, sequence checks, mandatory fields.
- Processing: automated calculations, matching (three-way match of PO, GRN and invoice), control totals.
- Output: exception reports, reconciliations of output with input.

If ITGCs are effective, an automated application control can be tested with a small sample (often a 'test of one' for each scenario) and the auditor can use **benchmarking** for later years where the program has not changed. If ITGCs are weak, the auditor cannot rely on automated controls without more testing, and moves towards substantive procedures.

lesson.heading: Audit trail, backups and IFC reporting
lesson.body:
- **Audit trail**: under the proviso to Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, from 1 April 2023 every company using accounting software must use software that records an audit trail of each transaction, creates an edit log of each change with the date of change, and does not allow the audit trail to be disabled.
- **Auditor's reporting**: Rule 11(g) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 requires the auditor to state whether the company used such software, whether the audit trail feature operated throughout the year for all relevant transactions, whether it was tampered with, and whether the audit trail has been preserved as per statutory requirements for record retention.
- **Backups**: books kept in electronic mode must have backups on servers physically located in India, on a daily basis.
- **Internal financial controls (IFC)**: section 143(3)(i) requires the auditor to state whether the company has adequate internal financial controls with reference to financial statements and their operating effectiveness. ICAI's Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls over Financial Reporting applies. Private companies meeting the exemption conditions (one person companies, small companies, and private companies with turnover below ₹50 crore as per the latest audited financial statements or aggregate borrowings below ₹25 crore, subject to no default in filing financial statements and annual returns) are exempt under MCA's June 2017 exemption notification.

lesson.heading: CAATs and data analytics
lesson.body:
Computer-assisted audit techniques (CAATs) include:

- **Test data**: the auditor processes dummy transactions through the client's system to check controls and processing.
- **Generalised audit software**: extracts and analyses client data (stratification, duplicates, gaps, ageing, recalculation).
- **Embedded audit modules and integrated test facility** for continuous auditing.

Data analytics in an audit:

| Use | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Risk assessment | Trend of monthly revenue by region; outliers |
| Journal entry testing | Entries posted on Sundays, by unusual users, round amounts, just below approval limits |
| Full-population testing | Recompute depreciation for every asset |
| Fraud indicators | Vendors sharing bank account numbers or addresses with employees; duplicate invoices |

The auditor must still evaluate the **completeness and accuracy of data** (information produced by the entity, IPE) before relying on analytics. Analytics complement, and do not replace, professional judgement.

lesson.heading: Common mistakes
lesson.body:
- Testing only application controls without assessing ITGCs that support them.
- Assuming a large sample is always needed for automated controls. With effective ITGCs, one instance per scenario can be enough.
- Treating Rule 11(g) reporting as a CARO clause. It is part of the main audit report under section 143(3)(j) read with Rule 11.
- Running analytics on client data without testing whether the data is complete and accurate.
- Writing that IFC reporting under section 143(3)(i) applies to every company. Exemptions exist for certain private companies.

keyPoints: Five components of internal control: control environment, risk assessment process, monitoring process, information system and communication, control activities.
ITGCs: access security, program change, program development, IT operations; they support automated application controls.
Audit trail software mandatory from 1 April 2023; auditor reports under Rule 11(g) on its operation, tampering and preservation.
Section 143(3)(i): auditor reports on adequacy and operating effectiveness of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements.
CAATs: test data, generalised audit software, embedded modules; test completeness and accuracy of client data first.

cases.title: Case: Orbit Retail Ltd
cases.body:
Orbit Retail Ltd runs 140 stores on a cloud ERP. During the FY 2025-26 audit, CA Farhan Sheikh notes:

| Area | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| Access | Two ERP developers have write access to the production environment |
| Change management | 11 program changes moved to production; 4 had no documented testing |
| Audit trail | The audit trail for the GL module was switched off from 1 to 20 November 2025 during an upgrade |
| Discounts | The ERP blocks discounts above 15% without a manager override code |
| Journals | 3,200 manual journal entries posted; 85 posted between 11 pm and 5 am |
| Backup | Daily backup kept on a server in Singapore only |

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an IT general control?
options: Three-way match of PO, GRN and invoice
Periodic review of user access rights
Credit limit check during sales order entry
Automated calculation of GST on invoices
questions.explanation: User access review is an access security ITGC that applies across applications. The others are application controls within specific processes.

questions.prompt: Under the proviso to Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, accounting software used by a company must:
options: Record an audit trail of each transaction with an edit log, and not allow the audit trail to be disabled
Be approved by the statutory auditor
Be an ERP licensed by MCA
questions.explanation: From 1 April 2023, accounting software must record an audit trail of every transaction, create an edit log of each change with the date, and ensure the audit trail cannot be disabled.

questions.prompt: An auditor processes dummy sales orders above the credit limit through the client's system to see whether they are rejected. This technique is:
questions.explanation: Test data means running auditor-prepared transactions through the client's live programs to check that controls work as designed.

questions.prompt: Under section 143(3)(i) of the Companies Act, 2013, the auditor reports on:
options: Adequacy and operating effectiveness of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements
questions.explanation: Section 143(3)(i) requires the auditor to state whether the company has adequate internal financial controls with reference to financial statements and the operating effectiveness of such controls.

questions.prompt: Developer access to production and untested program changes indicate weak ITGCs. What is the most appropriate effect on Farhan's plan to rely on the automated 15% discount control?
options: Rely on it with a test of one, since it is automated
Reliance is not supported without further work; test the control across the period or increase substantive procedures on discounts
Ignore discounts as they are routine
questions.explanation: A test of one is only enough when ITGCs (especially change management and access) are effective. Here the program could have been changed without approval, so the auditor must test more widely or move to substantive testing.

questions.prompt: How should the switching off of the GL audit trail from 1 to 20 November 2025 be reported?
options: In the main audit report under Rule 11(g): the audit trail did not operate throughout the year for all relevant transactions
Not reported, as it was during an upgrade
questions.explanation: Rule 11(g) requires the auditor to state whether the audit trail operated throughout the year for all relevant transactions. An 'upgrade' does not change the fact that it was disabled for 20 days.

questions.prompt: Which data analytics test best addresses the 85 journals posted between 11 pm and 5 am?
options: Filter journals by time, user and amount, and vouch the selected items for business rationale and approval
questions.explanation: Journal entry testing with filters on unusual timing, users and amounts responds to the management override risk under SA 240. Selected entries are then vouched for support and authorisation.

questions.prompt: Before using a client-generated report in data analytics, the auditor should evaluate whether the information is sufficiently complete and accurate.
questions.explanation: Information produced by the entity must be tested for completeness and accuracy (SA 500) before the auditor relies on it, whether in analytics or in manual procedures.

questions.prompt: Keeping the daily backup only on a server in Singapore meets the requirement for books maintained in electronic mode.
questions.explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 requires backups of books kept in electronic mode on servers physically located in India, on a daily basis.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are application controls? Select all that apply.
options: Limit check rejecting invoices above ₹5,00,000 without approval
Password complexity policy for the network
questions.explanation: Limit checks, sequence checks and three-way matching operate inside specific applications on transactions. Backup scheduling and network password policies are ITGCs.

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: the auditor's reporting on audit trail is required by Rule ___ of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014.
questions.explanation: Rule 11(g) covers use of accounting software with audit trail, its operation throughout the year, tampering and preservation.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'Since the client's ERP is a reputed international package, the auditor need not test IT general controls.'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- The reputation of the software does not show how the entity has configured, accessed and changed it.
- SA 315 requires the auditor to understand the IT environment and identify risks arising from the use of IT, including unauthorised access and changes.
- Automated controls and system reports are reliable only if ITGCs over access, change management and operations are effective.
- If the auditor plans to rely on automated controls or system-generated reports, ITGCs relevant to them must be evaluated and, where reliance is placed, tested.

Conclusion: ITGCs must be assessed regardless of the vendor's reputation.

questions.prompt: Explain the auditor's reporting responsibilities relating to audit trail in accounting software.
questions.answer:
- The proviso to Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 requires companies, from 1 April 2023, to use accounting software that records an audit trail of each transaction, creates an edit log of each change with the date, and does not allow the audit trail to be disabled.
- Under section 143(3)(j) read with Rule 11(g) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, the auditor states whether the company used such software, whether the audit trail feature operated throughout the year for all relevant transactions, whether there was any instance of tampering, and whether the audit trail has been preserved as per statutory record retention requirements.
- Where the feature was disabled for any period or module, the auditor reports the exception.
- The auditor also considers the effect on IFC reporting and on the risk assessment for journal entries.

questions.prompt: How can data analytics improve the quality of an audit? Give examples and limitations.
questions.answer:
Benefits:

- Tests entire populations rather than samples, for example recomputing interest on every loan account.
- Better risk assessment through trends, outliers and visualisations.
- Targeted journal entry testing on unusual times, users, round amounts and keywords.
- Fraud indicators such as duplicate payments or vendor-employee matches.

Limitations:

- Depends on complete and accurate data; IPE must be tested.
- Needs skilled staff and tools; results need investigation and judgement.
- Data privacy and confidentiality must be protected.
- Exceptions flagged are not misstatements until followed up.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'Every company must obtain a report from its auditor on internal financial controls under section 143(3)(i).'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- Section 143(3)(i) requires reporting on adequacy and operating effectiveness of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements.
- By MCA's exemption notification of 2017, the requirement does not apply to one person companies, small companies, and private companies with turnover below ₹50 crore as per the latest audited financial statements or aggregate borrowings from banks, financial institutions or bodies corporate below ₹25 crore at any point during the year, subject to the company not having defaulted in filing its financial statements under section 137 or annual return under section 92.
- Such private companies are therefore exempt.

Conclusion: IFC reporting is required for all companies other than those covered by the exemption.

chapters.title: Using the Work of Others and Special Audit Areas
chapters.summary: Using service organisations, other auditors, internal auditors and experts (SA 402, 600, 610, 620), and auditing estimates, related parties, subsequent events, going concern and written representations (SA 540, 550, 560, 570, 580).
chapters.applicableFor: May 2027 onward (ICAI new scheme, CA Final Paper 3)
chapters.lawAsOf: SA 402, 540, 550, 560, 570, 580, 600, 610 and 620 as issued by ICAI (extant SA 600; a revised SA 600 proposed by NFRA was not confirmed as notified at the time of writing)

lesson.heading: Using the work of others
lesson.body:
The auditor has **sole responsibility** for the opinion. Using others' work never reduces it.

| Standard | Who | What the auditor does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SA 402 | Service organisation (payroll bureau, cloud ERP host, custodian) | Understand services used; obtain a **Type 1 report** (description and design of controls at a date) or **Type 2 report** (design and operating effectiveness over a period) from the service auditor; evaluate its period and scope |
| SA 600 | Other auditor auditing a component (subsidiary, branch, division) | Principal auditor assesses own participation, informs the other auditor of reporting requirements and independence needs, considers the other auditor's competence, and performs procedures to obtain sufficient evidence that the work is adequate |
| SA 610 | Internal audit function | Evaluate objectivity, competence and systematic and disciplined approach; decide areas where its work can be used; perform procedures on that work |
| SA 620 | Auditor's expert (valuer, actuary, engineer) | Evaluate competence, capabilities and objectivity; agree scope in writing; evaluate the adequacy of the expert's work |

Reporting points:

- SA 620: the auditor does not refer to the expert in an **unmodified** report unless required by law. If referred to in a modified report, the report states that the reference does not reduce the auditor's responsibility.
- SA 600 (extant): where the principal auditor uses the work of another auditor, the report discloses this, typically in an Other Matter paragraph stating the amounts involved.
- NFRA has proposed a revised SA 600 aligned with ISA 600 (Revised). At the time of writing its notification and effective date were not confirmed; check ICAI and NFRA updates.

lesson.heading: Estimates and related parties (SA 540, SA 550)
lesson.body:
**SA 540** (accounting estimates): understand how management makes estimates (method, assumptions, data), review the outcome of prior-period estimates retrospectively, and respond by one or more of: testing management's process, developing the auditor's own point estimate or range, or using events up to the date of the report. Watch for **management bias** (consistent optimism or pessimism).

**SA 550** (related parties):

- Understand related party relationships and transactions, and controls over authorising them.
- Stay alert for undisclosed related parties when inspecting records (bank and legal confirmations, minutes, shareholder registers).
- If management asserts that a related party transaction was on **arm's length** terms, the auditor obtains sufficient evidence about that assertion.
- Under the Companies Act, 2013, check approvals under section 188 (and section 177 for audit committee approval). CARO 2020 clause (xiii) requires reporting on compliance with sections 177 and 188 and disclosure in financial statements.

lesson.heading: Subsequent events (SA 560) and written representations (SA 580)
lesson.body:
SA 560 deals with three periods:

| Period | Auditor's duty |
| --- | --- |
| Date of financial statements to date of auditor's report | **Active**: perform procedures to identify events needing adjustment or disclosure (inquiry, minutes, latest interims) |
| After report date, before financial statements are issued | **Passive**: no duty to search; if a fact becomes known that would have caused amendment, discuss with management, and if amended, extend procedures and issue a new report |
| After financial statements are issued | Passive; if a fact becomes known, discuss, and if management revises, issue a new report with an Emphasis of Matter. If management does not act, take steps to prevent reliance |

Adjusting events give evidence of conditions at the balance sheet date (customer insolvency after year end that existed at year end). Non-adjusting events arise after it (a fire after year end), and are disclosed if material.

**SA 580**: written representations are dated as near as practicable to, but **not after**, the date of the auditor's report, and cover all periods referred to in the report. They are necessary evidence but not sufficient on their own. If management does not provide the representation that it has fulfilled its responsibility for preparing the financial statements and for providing information, or if the auditor doubts management's integrity so those representations are unreliable, the auditor **disclaims** an opinion.

lesson.heading: Going concern (SA 570)
lesson.body:
Indicators: net liability position, defaults on loans, negative operating cash flows, loss of a major market or key customer, labour difficulties, pending legal cases with claims the entity cannot meet.

The auditor evaluates management's assessment (normally at least 12 months from the date of the financial statements), management's plans for future actions, and obtains written representations on those plans.

| Situation | Opinion |
| --- | --- |
| Going concern appropriate, material uncertainty exists, **adequately disclosed** | Unmodified, with a separate section 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' |
| Material uncertainty, **not adequately disclosed** | Qualified or adverse |
| Use of going concern basis **inappropriate** | Adverse |
| Management unwilling to make or extend its assessment | Consider the effect; may lead to qualified or disclaimer |

The MURGC section is not a Key Audit Matter, even for listed entities, although it is referred to in the KAM section.

keyPoints: Using others' work (SA 402, 600, 610, 620) never reduces the auditor's sole responsibility for the opinion.
SA 402: Type 1 report = design at a date; Type 2 report = design and operating effectiveness over a period.
SA 620: no reference to the expert in an unmodified report unless required by law.
SA 560: active duty up to report date; passive duty thereafter.
SA 580: representations dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the report date; refusal of fundamental representations leads to a disclaimer.
SA 570: adequate disclosure of material uncertainty = unmodified opinion with a MURGC section; inappropriate basis = adverse.

cases.title: Case: Zenith Auto Components Ltd
cases.body:
CA Pradeep Nair audits the standalone and consolidated financial statements of Zenith Auto Components Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2026. The auditor's report is planned for 25 May 2026.

| Item | Fact |
| --- | --- |
| Subsidiary | Zenith Castings Pvt Ltd, whose assets are 18% of consolidated assets, is audited by another firm |
| Land revaluation | Land revalued at ₹42 crore based on a report by a registered valuer engaged by management |
| Customer | Main customer Kirti Motors, owing ₹6.2 crore at year end, filed for insolvency on 22 April 2026; it was in severe financial difficulty since January 2026 |
| Fire | Fire at the Nashik warehouse on 2 May 2026 destroyed inventory of ₹3.5 crore (not insured) |
| Borrowings | The company defaulted on term loan instalments in February and March 2026; the bank has not recalled the loan; disclosure is adequate |
| Representations | The MD refuses to sign the representation that all information and access were provided |

questions.prompt: A Type 2 report under SA 402 covers:
options: Only the description of the service organisation's system
Description and design of controls at a specified date
Description, design and operating effectiveness of controls over a specified period
Financial statements of the service organisation
questions.explanation: A Type 2 report adds the service auditor's opinion on operating effectiveness over a period, which supports reliance on controls. A Type 1 report covers only description and design at a date.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the factors under SA 610 for deciding whether the work of the internal audit function can be used?
options: Application of a systematic and disciplined approach
The internal audit fee being lower than the external audit fee
questions.explanation: SA 610 evaluates objectivity (organisational status), competence and a systematic and disciplined approach including quality control. Fees are not a criterion.

questions.prompt: Under SA 580, written representations should be dated:
options: As near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report
Any date within 60 days after the report
On the date of the AGM
questions.explanation: Representations support evidence obtained up to the report date, so SA 580 requires them to be dated as near as practicable to, but not after, that date.

questions.prompt: Management says a sale of machinery to a director's firm was on arm's length terms. Under SA 550, the auditor should:
options: Accept the assertion as management's responsibility
Obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the assertion
Ignore it if the amount is below ₹10,00,000
Report it to the Central Government
questions.explanation: SA 550 requires evidence supporting an arm's length assertion in the disclosures, for example comparing terms with similar unrelated-party transactions or market data.

questions.prompt: How should the receivable from Kirti Motors (₹6.2 crore) and the warehouse fire (₹3.5 crore) be treated?
options: Kirti Motors is adjusting (condition existed at year end); fire is non-adjusting and disclosed if material
Kirti Motors is non-adjusting; fire is adjusting
questions.explanation: The customer was in financial difficulty before year end, so the insolvency gives evidence of a condition at the balance sheet date and needs a loss allowance. The fire happened after year end, so it is disclosed, not adjusted.

questions.prompt: Given the loan defaults with adequate disclosure, and assuming the going concern basis remains appropriate, the report should include:
options: An unmodified opinion with a 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' section
questions.explanation: Under SA 570, when the going concern basis is appropriate and a material uncertainty is adequately disclosed, the opinion is unmodified and a separate MURGC section is added.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of the MD refusing to provide the representation on providing all information and access?
options: Qualified opinion limited to the land revaluation
Disclaimer of opinion, after discussing with management and re-evaluating integrity
Unmodified opinion with Emphasis of Matter
No effect, as other evidence is available
questions.explanation: SA 580 requires a disclaimer when management does not provide the representations on its responsibilities for preparing financial statements and providing information, because these cannot be replaced by other evidence.

questions.prompt: An auditor who uses the work of an auditor's expert may refer to the expert in an unmodified auditor's report to show shared responsibility.
questions.explanation: SA 620 prohibits reference to the expert in an unmodified report unless required by law, because it could be misunderstood as dividing responsibility. The auditor has sole responsibility.

questions.prompt: Pradeep may use the valuer's report on land, but must evaluate the valuer's competence, capabilities and objectivity as management's expert under SA 500.
questions.explanation: The valuer was engaged by management, so it is a management's expert. SA 500 requires the auditor to evaluate competence, capabilities and objectivity, understand the work, and evaluate its appropriateness as audit evidence.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are going concern indicators under SA 570? Select all that apply.
options: Change of statutory auditor on rotation
questions.explanation: Net current liabilities, loan defaults and loss of a key customer are financial or operating indicators listed in SA 570. Auditor rotation and higher dividends are not indicators.

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: the standard on auditing that deals with using the work of an auditor's expert is SA ___.
questions.explanation: SA 620, Using the Work of an Auditor's Expert.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'After signing the audit report on 25 May 2026, the auditor learns on 10 June 2026, before the financial statements are issued, that a major debtor had gone bankrupt before year end. Since the report is signed, he has no responsibility.'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- SA 560: after the report date, the auditor has no obligation to perform procedures, but if a fact becomes known that, had it been known at the report date, may have caused him to amend the report, he must act.
- He discusses the matter with management and TCWG, determines whether the financial statements need amendment, and inquires how management intends to address it.
- If management amends the financial statements, he extends procedures to the new date and issues a new report dated not earlier than the approval of the amended statements.
- If management does not amend and the report has not been provided to the entity, he modifies the opinion; if already provided, he notifies management and TCWG not to issue the statements and takes action to prevent reliance.

Conclusion: the auditor has a responsibility once the fact becomes known.

questions.prompt: Explain the auditor's reporting responsibilities under SA 570 when events cast significant doubt on going concern.
questions.answer:
- The auditor evaluates management's assessment, its plans and their feasibility, and obtains written representations.
- If the going concern basis is appropriate but a material uncertainty exists and is adequately disclosed: unmodified opinion with a separate section headed 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern', drawing attention to the note and stating the opinion is not modified.
- If the disclosure is inadequate: qualified or adverse opinion as appropriate, with the basis section stating that a material uncertainty exists.
- If the financial statements are prepared on a going concern basis that is inappropriate: adverse opinion.
- If management is unwilling to make or extend its assessment when requested: consider the effect on the report.
- The auditor communicates the events or conditions to TCWG.

questions.prompt: Comment with reasons: 'The principal auditor of a holding company can accept the other auditor's report on a subsidiary without any procedures, because the other auditor is also a Chartered Accountant.'
questions.answer:
Not correct.

- Under SA 600, the principal auditor must consider the professional competence of the other auditor in the context of the specific assignment.
- He advises the other auditor of independence requirements, the use to be made of the work, and the reporting requirements, and obtains confirmation of compliance.
- He performs procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence that the other auditor's work is adequate, such as discussions, review of a written summary of procedures, or review of working papers, depending on the circumstances.
- Being a member of ICAI is relevant to competence but does not remove these requirements.

Conclusion: some procedures are always required before using the other auditor's work.

questions.prompt: Explain how the auditor responds to the risks in accounting estimates under SA 540.
questions.answer:
- Obtain an understanding of the requirements of the framework, how management identifies the need for estimates, the method, assumptions and data, and controls over the process.
- Review the outcome of prior-period estimates (retrospective review) to identify bias and evaluate the process.
- Respond by one or more of: obtaining evidence from events up to the report date; testing how management made the estimate (method, assumptions, data); developing the auditor's own point estimate or range.
- For estimates with high estimation uncertainty, evaluate the reasonableness of significant assumptions and the adequacy of disclosures.
- Evaluate indicators of possible management bias and obtain written representations on reasonableness of significant assumptions.

chapters.title: Completion, Audit Reports and CARO 2020
